To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Prdm12 is required to generate V1 interneuronal cells in the vertebrate spinal cord, that Prdm12 expression is regulated by retinoic acid, Pax6, and by cross-repressive interactions of Prdm12 with Dbx1/6, and that vertebrate Prd12 proteins, but not their amphioxus orthologs, recruit the G9a H3K9me2/3 methyltransferase.
Prdm12 is a key determinant for the specification of the vertebrate V1 interneuronal cell fate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the development and evolution of the nervous system in vertebrates.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of the nervous system in the frog, Xenopus.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of the vertebrate hindbrain and spinal chord, in particular the specification of the V1 inhibitory interneuron subtype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vertebrate Prdm gene family has been involved in neural crest and V1 interneuronal specification since the split of the cephalo- and vertebrate lineages.
Prdm12 is a general V1 determinant in vertebrates, and that this function is not shared with the Prdm12 protein of amphioxus.
Prdm12 acts as a general determinant for V1 interneuronal specification in vertebrates, but not in amphioxus, through cross-repressive actions with Dbx1, Nkx6,1/2 and G9a.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Prdm12 is a key regulator of the specification of V1 interneuronal cells.
Prdm12 is a general determinant of vertebrate V1 interneuronal specification, at least in the hindbrain and in the spinal cord.
the vertebrate Prdm family of genes have been co-opted to specify V1 interneuronal fate, at least partially, through a cross-repressive network with Dbx1, Nkx6 and Pax6.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Prdm12 acts as a determinant of the V1 cell fate through cross-repressive mechanisms with Dbx1/Nkx6 genes and that this function has been acquired after the divergence between vertebrates and cephalochords.
Prdm12 is an important regulator of vertebrate V1 cell fate and that its function might be specific to vertebrates.
Prdm12 specifies the V1 cell fate by directly represssing Dbx1 and the related Nkx6 gene, a function that has only been acquired in vertebrates.
